prize_parts.citation: for establishing, through measurements on engineered proteins, the physical principles of long-range electron tunnelling and hopping in biological molecules

statement.case_for: Gray and Winkler turned the question of how electrons cross tens of angstroms of protein into a quantitative, physical result. Using ruthenium-modified proteins and laser-triggered kinetics, they measured rates against distance and driving force, tied the data to Marcus theory, and showed that the protein matrix and tunnelling pathways set the rate. Later they added multistep hopping through tryptophan and tyrosine radicals as a protective and functional mechanism. This is the physical basis of respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer, and it is a mechanism stated in physical terms and backed by time-resolved kinetics, not a description of a pathway. The picture has stood for decades and is now textbook material, so the question is one of attribution and weighing, not of maturity. Gray and Winkler are the clearest experimental leaders of the line, which makes a two-person citation credible.
statement.case_against: Support is thin. Only I ranked B026 first and no colleague ranked it at all, so it may reflect my own field's bias more than the committee's view. Credit is also shared. Dutton and Moser's natural-system work on the distance dependence of electron transfer, and the pathway theory of Beratan and Onuchic, are close parallel claims, and a two-name prize omits them. A fair review would also ask how much beyond the 1992 Marcus prize this adds, and whether the result is a mechanism that changed other chemists' practice as widely as the methods and tools that colleagues rank higher.

responses.point: Johan ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first, regards Buchwald and Hartwig as the clean pair, treats Kosugi as a conceptually distinct precursor, and calls the recognition overdue given the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: I accept that the case is strong on impact and maturity, and with three first-place votes it is the natural reference point. My reservation is attribution. Kosugi's tin-amide aminations (1983) and Migita's work are the actual priority record, and what Buchwald and Hartwig added is the ligand-controlled catalytic version with tin removed. I think the committee needs the expert report to say whether that step is a new reaction or a development of an existing one before we assume a two-name citation. The distance from the 2010 prize also needs a concrete argument, because the cross-coupling mechanistic framework is shared. If the report supports the two names, I would not oppose B057, and it is my first alternative.

responses.point: Heiner ranks base editing first as a clear, principled new capability with a defined chemical mechanism, rapid adoption and early therapeutic use, and sees Liu with Komor and Gaudelli as defensible.
responses.response: The chemistry is clear and I respect the mechanism, deamination on DNA without a double-strand break. I do not agree that the maturity question is settled. The first report is about a decade old, clinical safety and off-target deamination data are still accruing, and the 2020 prize for programmable DNA cleavage gives the field a close predecessor. On attribution, I would not put two trainees alongside Liu without evidence that they conceived the work and did not carry out the experiments. Priority is also not clean, because Nishida and Kondo reported a cytidine deaminase fusion independently in 2016. I would want the expert report to separate Liu's conceptual leadership from the other two strands before supporting this as the prize.

responses.point: Emma ranks biomolecular condensates first as a new concept of cellular organisation grounded in physical chemistry, while acknowledging that the field is about a decade old and that debate persists over which structures are thermodynamic phases.
responses.response: I share the interest in the physical-chemical framing and agree it is the most conceptually original proposal on the list. My concern is the one you raise yourself. Whether a cellular body is a demixed phase or a different kind of assembly has not been settled by experiment, and mechanism claims in cells often rest on indirect tests. A prize now would honour a framework whose boundaries are still being drawn. The three-name limit is also tight, since Pappu and Mittag supplied the sequence grammar and physics that make the idea quantitative. I would treat this as a strong candidate for a later year and would want to hear what the expert report says on in vivo evidence.

responses.point: Daniel ranks targeted protein degradation first as a new modality with a clear molecular design principle, and concedes that the molecular-glue strand and the lack of an approved degrader complicate credit and timing.
responses.response: I agree that the design principle is real and that the field is substantial. Our two difficulties overlap. Crews and Deshaies, Ciulli, and Handa and Ito represent two partly distinct discoveries, the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism for thalidomide and glues, and a three-person limit cannot honour both. With no approved PROTAC, a prize now would be for the concept and the promise. If the committee wants a mechanistic chemistry award, I find the better-established cases to be those with a settled attribution and a stable mechanism, though I would not rule this out for the future.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report confirms Gray and Winkler as the leading attributable pair, given Dutton and Moser, Beratan and Onuchic, and the relationship to the 1992 Marcus prize
Whether the committee will treat a biophysical mechanism with no other first-place support as competitive against the broader methods and tools ranked by colleagues
How the expert report resolves the Kosugi and Migita priority question for C-N coupling
Whether clinical and safety data for base editing and targeted degradation will change the maturity assessment by the time of the final ballot
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates, since none are Stockholm University colleagues or collaborators. I note for transparency that my own research field in respiratory-chain electron and proton transfer is close to B026, which is a scientific interest and not an institutional connection, and that I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose work is not on this shortlist.
